name: io.github.notformal/adsbeast
title: ADS Beast
description: Ad account audits, analytics, leads and campaign changes that run only from an approved preview.

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: The API key in use: name, organization, scopes, and whether it can propose changes. A 403 from any tool means a missing scope listed here.

tools.name: get_new_leads
tools.description: Leads with contacts, form answers and attribution (UTM, click ids, form, campaign). updated_since (ISO-8601) gives only new or changed ones; page with next_offset while has_more.

updated_since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp, for example 2026-06-13T18:00:00Z. Returns leads updated at or after it, which is the last-sync value for incremental pulls.

since.description: ISO-8601 timestamp. Returns leads created at or after it, ignoring later edits to older leads.

client_id.description: Restrict to one client. A client of another organization answers 404.

source.description: Where the lead came from, for example 'meta_lead_form' for Meta instant forms or 'public_form' for a website form.

stage.description: Restrict to one pipeline stage. One of: new, contacted, qualified, proposal_sent, negotiation, won, lost.

limit.description: Page size. Clamped into 1..5000 before the request. A page is also cut to fit the response size limit; when the reply has has_more = true, call again with offset = next_offset.

offset.description: Pagination offset. Use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: get_lead
tools.description: Return a single lead by its ADS Beast id with every field the record holds, including email, phone, qualification answers, attribution and its current pipeline stage.

lead_id.description: ADS Beast id of the lead, as returned by get_new_leads.

tools.name: list_lead_forms
tools.description: Return the lead forms recorded for this organization, which maps the form ids and source keys that appear on a lead to readable form names.

platform.description: Restrict to one platform, for example meta.

limit.description: Forms per page, newest first. Each form carries its questions, so keep pages small.

offset.description: Forms to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: lead_pipeline_stats
tools.description: Return aggregate lead counts by pipeline stage over a recent window, for the whole organization or for one client.

days.description: Length of the window in days, counted back from now. At most one year.

tools.name: lead_outcome_contract
tools.description: Return the field names and outcome values that push_lead_outcomes accepts, as the server currently defines them.

tools.name: update_lead
tools.description: Change fields of one lead (notes, assignee, contacts, stage). Only supplied keys are written; an unwritable key is refused with the list of writable ones.

lead_id.description: ADS Beast id of the lead to change.

fields.description: Object of field name to new value, for example {"stage": "qualified", "notes": "Called back"}. Fields not listed keep their current value. Writable fields: assigned_to, company_name, contact_email, contact_name, contact_phone, estimated_monthly_budget, estimated_monthly_fee, expected_close_date, last_contact_at, lost_reason, notes, probability_pct, proposal_id, source, stage, tags, website.

tools.name: move_lead_stage
tools.description: Move one lead to a different pipeline stage. Unlike setting the stage through update_lead, this also remaps the lead's close probability to the value configured for the new stage.

lead_id.description: ADS Beast id of the lead to move.

stage.description: Stage to move the lead into.

tools.name: push_lead_outcomes
tools.description: Write lead outcomes back so ad platforms learn which leads sold. A row names a lead (lead_id, email or phone) and its outcome. dry_run (default true) writes nothing; run it first. Unmatched rows are skipped unless create_missing; the stage follows unless update_stage is false.

rows.description: Outcome rows, for example [{"lead_id": 812, "outcome": "won", "reason": "signed"}]. For outcome paid add value (amount), currency (ISO 4217) and plan, e.g. {"external_lead_id": "u-1", "outcome": "paid", "value": 690, "currency": "UAH", "plan": "Pro"}. Accepted field names and outcome values come from lead_outcome_contract.

create_missing.description: Create a new lead for a row that matches none. Off by default: a typo in an email must not insert a record.

update_stage.description: Move a matched lead's pipeline stage to match the outcome, for example to won or lost.

dry_run.description: True reports what would change and writes nothing. False applies the rows.

source_system.description: Name of the system the outcomes came from, recorded on each row.

client_id.description: Client the rows belong to. Optional with a key bound to one client - that client is used.

tools.name: list_campaigns
tools.description: Return campaigns from every connected advertising platform in one list, with their status, budget and platform ids. Archived campaigns are left out unless include_archived is true.

platform.description: Restrict to one platform. Omit for all platforms.

limit.description: Page size. Clamped into 1..2000 before the request. A page is also cut to fit the response size limit; when the reply has has_more = true, call again with offset = next_offset.

offset.description: Pagination offset. The reply carries total.

tools.name: get_campaign
tools.description: Return a single campaign by its ADS Beast id with its settings, budget, status and the native id it has on its platform.

campaign_id.description: ADS Beast id of the campaign, as returned by list_campaigns.

tools.name: campaign_dashboard_summary
tools.description: Return spend, conversions and delivery health aggregated across the whole organization. The endpoint takes no filter and always covers every client; per-client figures come from list_campaigns with a client_id.

tools.name: list_clients
tools.description: Return the clients of this organization with their budgets, status and connected advertising accounts. A long list comes back as a page {result, total, has_more, next_offset}.

offset.description: Clients to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: get_client
tools.description: Return a single client by its ADS Beast id: profile, budget, goals and connected advertising accounts.

client_id.description: ADS Beast id of the client, as returned by list_clients.

tools.name: list_reports
tools.description: Return the client reports already generated in ADS Beast, newest first, with their type, period and client.

report_type.description: Restrict to one kind of report, for example monthly or audit.

limit.description: Reports per page, newest first. Each report carries its sections, so keep pages small.

offset.description: Reports to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: list_alerts
tools.description: Return the performance and delivery alerts raised by the ADS Beast monitoring agents, with their severity, the client or campaign they concern and whether they have been read or resolved.

is_read.description: False returns only alerts nobody has read yet.

is_resolved.description: False returns only alerts that are still open.

alert_type.description: Restrict to one kind of alert.

campaign_id.description: Restrict to one campaign.

limit.description: Page size, newest first. Clamped into 1..5000 before the request. A page is also cut to fit the response size limit; when the reply has has_more = true, call again with offset = next_offset.

offset.description: Alerts to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: alerts_unread_count
tools.description: How many live alerts are unread, as one number; an alert whose condition cleared is not counted. Cheaper than list_alerts for the count.

tools.name: list_tasks
tools.description: Return the team tasks recorded in ADS Beast with their status, priority, assignee and the client they belong to.

limit.description: Page size. Clamped into 1..500 before the request. A page is also cut to fit the response size limit; when the reply has has_more = true, call again with offset = next_offset.

offset.description: Pagination offset. The reply carries total.

tools.name: list_outreach_campaigns
tools.description: Page of email outreach campaigns, newest first: status, sender, offer pack, legal basis, daily limit. Walk pages with offset = next_offset. The letter is body_preview and body_chars; include_body = true gives the full text.

offset.description: Campaigns to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

include_body.description: True returns each campaign's full letter (body_template); the page is then cut to fit the response size limit.

tools.name: outreach_campaign_check
tools.description: Run the pre-launch check of one email outreach campaign: who may be emailed under its legal basis, why the others are blocked (consent, personal mailbox, country, unsubscribed), and sender problems. Blocker issues stop the campaign from being activated.

campaign_id.description: Email campaign id.

tools.name: list_offer_packs
tools.description: Return the offer packs outreach copy is built from: built-in samples and this organization's own client packs, with brand, languages, niches, the facts the copy relies on and how many errors or warnings the last check found.

offset.description: Packs to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: list_social_campaigns
tools.description: Return the Instagram/TikTok/Facebook prospecting campaigns: offer, platforms, cities with message language, daily manual-send cap.

offset.description: Campaigns to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: get_social_queue
tools.description: Next profiles to message by hand, best first, within today's cap: link, signals, the drafted first message (no link) and the follow-up with a tracked link. Sends nothing.

campaign_id.description: Social campaign id.

tools.name: update_social_prospect
tools.description: Record what happened after a hand-sent message (sent, replied, registered, declined, do_not_contact, skipped, new to undo). 'sent' is refused past today's cap. Messages no one.

note.description: Free note, e.g. what they answered.

tools.name: list_webhook_events
tools.description: Return the event names an outbound webhook can subscribe to, for example lead.created, with what each one carries.

tools.name: list_webhooks
tools.description: Return the outbound webhook endpoints registered for this organization, the events each one receives and its current delivery state.

offset.description: Webhooks to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: create_webhook
tools.description: Register a URL ADS Beast calls on a chosen event until it is removed; without client_id it covers every client. Deliveries carry an HMAC in X-ADS-Beast-Signature and are retried; the generated secret is not returned, so pass secret_key if the receiver verifies signatures.

name.description: Label for the webhook in the ADS Beast interface.

client_id.description: Limit deliveries to one client's events. Omitted, the webhook receives every client's events in the organization.

secret_key.description: Signing secret for X-ADS-Beast-Signature, chosen by you. Omit to let ADS Beast generate one that this tool will not echo back.

url.description: Absolute http or https address of the receiving endpoint. Every matching event is sent to it.

events.description: Event names to subscribe to, for example ["lead.created"]. The available names come from list_webhook_events.

tools.name: seo_publish_safety
tools.description: Ask before publishing or scheduling an article: articles allowed today and published, whether publishing is paused and why, indexed vs kept-out articles. Start at 2 a day, +1 a week up to 6; one language version of a topic a day. Never plan around the limits.

client_id.description: The site's client id; omit for the organization overview.

tools.name: list_proposals
tools.description: Change proposals waiting for a person (status pending by default), or their history. Each proposal shows what would change, why, and who proposed it.

status.description: pending, approved, rejected, executed, expired or failed.

limit.description: Proposals per page. A page is also cut to fit the response size limit; when the reply has has_more = true, call again with offset = next_offset.

offset.description: Proposals to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: propose_campaign_change
tools.description: Create a change proposal for a campaign. Nothing changes in the ad account until a person approves the proposal in ADS Beast or in Telegram; the proposal expires on its own if nobody decides. State the reason with the numbers behind it.

campaign_id.description: ADS Beast campaign id (from list_campaigns).

reason.description: Why - with the figures the person should check.

new_budget.description: New monthly budget in the account currency; change_budget only.

tools.name: reject_proposal
tools.description: Reject a pending proposal with a short reason. Returns the proposal id and its new status.

tools.name: list_campaign_types
tools.description: Campaign types an assistant may draft per platform: the campaign_type key, objective, tracking, bid strategies and under 'fields' what a draft needs with character limits. structure_check 'full' (Google Search, Meta) is the builder's own pre-publish check; 'basic' only common checks.

platform.description: Only this platform's types. Without it every type is listed.

tools.name: list_campaign_drafts
tools.description: Builder drafts, newest first: name, platform, type, status, budget, counts, whether an assistant made it or it was published, and the link. A client-bound key sees its client only.

client_id.description: Only this client's builds (id from list_clients).

limit.description: Builds per page. A page is also cut to fit the response size limit; when the reply has has_more = true, call again with offset = next_offset.

offset.description: Builds to skip; use next_offset from the previous page.

tools.name: get_campaign_draft
tools.description: One build and a fresh validation: 'problems' block publishing, 'warnings' do not, 'launch_blockers' say why a person could not publish now, 'not_checked_here' what only publishing checks.

draft_id.description: Build id from list_campaign_drafts or create_campaign_draft.

tools.name: create_campaign_draft
tools.description: Create a campaign DRAFT in the builder: type, geo, languages, budget, ad groups with keywords or audiences, ads, landing. Nothing reaches the platform. Returns draft id, builder_url and what blocks publishing; the draft is saved anyway. Call list_campaign_types first.

campaign_type.description: Type key from list_campaign_types, for example google.search or meta.leads_website.

name.description: Campaign name a person will see in the builder.

landing_url.description: https landing for ads without final_url.

ad_groups.description: Fields and limits per type: list_campaign_types.

items.description: Search: headlines[], descriptions[], path1, path2, final_url, sitelinks[{text, description1, description2, url}], callouts[]. Social: primary_text, headline, description, cta, image_url, final_url.

audience.description: Social types: age_min, age_max, genders, interests, placements, custom_audiences, allow_broad_audience + broad_audience_reason.

conversion.description: Meta leads/sales: {type: 'website', pixel_id, event} or {type: 'lead_form', lead_form_id}.

extra.description: page_id, instagram_actor_id, dsa_beneficiary, dsa_payor, structured_snippets, search_partners, display_network, geo_target_type, vertical, devices, job_titles, industries, cities, regions.

tools.name: update_campaign_draft
tools.description: Replace fields of an unpublished draft made by create_campaign_draft; each field replaces the stored one whole. Returns a fresh validation. A person's draft or a published build is refused.

landing_url.description: https landing for ads without final_url.

ad_groups.description: Fields and limits per type: list_campaign_types.

items.description: Search: headlines[], descriptions[], path1, path2, final_url, sitelinks[{text, description1, description2, url}], callouts[]. Social: primary_text, headline, description, cta, image_url, final_url.

audience.description: Social types: age_min, age_max, genders, interests, placements, custom_audiences, allow_broad_audience + broad_audience_reason.

conversion.description: Meta leads/sales: {type: 'website', pixel_id, event} or {type: 'lead_form', lead_form_id}.

extra.description: page_id, instagram_actor_id, dsa_beneficiary, dsa_payor, structured_snippets, search_partners, display_network, geo_target_type, vertical, devices, job_titles, industries, cities, regions.

tools.name: create_campaign_paused
tools.description: One call: builder draft, its checks (limits, policy, niche gate, account, write policy), a live-account rehearsal and a key-bound publish request. After a person approves, it is created PAUSED; only a person switches it on (how_to_launch). Google video is refused: its API cannot create it.

reason.description: Why, with numbers (shown to the approver).

draft.description: Fields of create_campaign_draft: geo, languages, daily_budget, ad_groups, ...

tools.name: dashboard_tiles
tools.description: Tiles per ad account for N days, each in its own currency; null = not measured. share_url: a live /d/ link to show in full.

tools.name: get_platform_connect_link
tools.description: A signed link to this workspace's Google or Meta sign-in: 15 min, any signed-in member, not single-use. The person signs in on the platform's page; the link connects nothing itself.

tools.name: list_connected_platforms
tools.description: Per platform: connected through the API and signed in, account names. Call it after get_platform_connect_link.

tools.name: get_autonomy_mode
tools.description: Each client's mode: watch (nothing is written), propose (a person approves every change) or auto (reversible changes apply inside the policy, with undo and the emergency stop). Only a person changes it.

tools.name: get_agency_kit
tools.description: One client's knowledge pack: who they are, accounts and campaigns with 30 days of results, leads by stage, KPI goals, write policy, methodology, prompts. Read it first. No contacts or keys.

tools.name: client_overview
tools.description: One client with its campaigns, key metrics and goals.

tools.name: client_action_plan
tools.description: The action plan from the client's latest weekly deep-dive audit: findings labelled confirmed, inferred or hypothesis, open change proposals and open tasks.

tools.name: client_goals
tools.description: KPI goals (ROAS, CPA, CTR, CPC) with target, current value, progress and status. Without client_id: goals of every client.

tools.name: client_data_freshness
tools.description: When each client and platform was last synced. Call it before a deep analysis so stale data is named as stale.

tools.name: client_memory_search
tools.description: Search the facts, decisions, preferences and brand notes ADS Beast has stored about clients.

query.description: What to look for, in plain words.

tools.name: client_history_search
tools.description: Full-text search over a client's earlier reports, audits and analyses.

tools.name: client_landing_scan
tools.description: Read a landing page and extract its headline, offer, selling points, calls to action, keywords and tone. Without url, the client's own site is used. AI: 1 AI request.

tools.name: client_market_analysis
tools.description: The stored market analysis of a client: summary, competitor matrix, audience signals and the draft campaign strategy.

section.description: all, summary, competitors, audience, strategy or insights.

tools.name: client_market_analysis_run
tools.description: Crawl the client's site, find and analyse competitors and build a market intelligence report. Takes minutes; read the result with client_market_analysis. AI: 1 AI request.

force.description: true re-runs even when a fresh report exists.

tools.name: client_market_intel_search
tools.description: Semantic search over a client's indexed market data: its site, competitor profiles and the market report.

tools.name: client_market_simulation
tools.description: Status and report of the multi-agent market simulations requested for a client.

tools.name: analytics_summary
tools.description: Spend, CTR, CPA and ROAS of one client over a period. Money is reported in the account currency and never summed across currencies.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

tools.name: analytics_compare_periods
tools.description: Percentage change of every KPI between the current period and the one before it, by platform, with what got worse and what improved.

current_days.description: Length of the current period in days.

previous_days.description: Length of the preceding period in days.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

tools.name: analytics_forecast
tools.description: Projection of CPA, ROAS and spend 7 and 30 days ahead from the current trend. A projection, not a promise: it extrapolates the last 14-30 days.

campaign_id.description: ADS Beast id from list_campaigns, not the platform's.

tools.name: analytics_forecast_warnings
tools.description: Campaigns expected to break a KPI target within days, from a linear trend.

tools.name: analytics_attribution
tools.description: Time-decay multi-touch attribution for a client's campaigns: attributed conversions, attributed CPA and the lift against last click.

tools.name: analytics_portfolio
tools.description: Cross-client analysis of the whole portfolio: best and worst performers, platform trends, total spend. Takes up to a minute. AI: 1 AI request.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

tools.name: analytics_cross_client_insights
tools.description: Patterns and anomalies across clients: platforms that sag for most of them, shared niche problems, who outperforms.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

tools.name: analytics_kpi_health
tools.description: Quick status of all active campaigns: how many are on target and how many need attention.

tools.name: analytics_growth_opportunities
tools.description: Campaigns ready to scale: ROAS well above target, CPA well below target, or budget left unused.

min_roas_multiplier.description: ROAS-to-target ratio that counts as ready to scale, for example 1.5.

tools.name: analytics_benchmarks
tools.description: Reference CTR, CPC, CPA and ROAS ranges for a platform and niche. Benchmarks are orientation, not a verdict on one account.

niche.description: Business niche or industry, in plain words.

tools.name: analytics_agency_briefing
tools.description: Morning briefing for the workspace: critical alerts, today's tasks and what needs attention now.

tools.name: analytics_media_plan
tools.description: A sourced chain of planning numbers for a campaign type: CPM, reach, clicks, CPC, conversion rate, conversions, CPA, break-even and three scenarios. Every figure is labelled with where it comes from.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

objective_or_type.description: Goal or campaign type: leads, sales, traffic, or a key from campaign_type_coverage.

monthly_budget.description: Monthly budget in the stated currency, whole units.

currency.description: ISO currency code of the budget.

niche.description: Business niche or industry, in plain words.

avg_order_value.description: Average order value, for revenue and break-even.

gross_margin_pct.description: Gross margin in percent, for break-even.

num_objects.description: How many ad sets or ad groups share the budget.

tools.name: analytics_ab_tests
tools.description: A/B tests with their status and interim results.

campaign_id.description: ADS Beast id from list_campaigns, not the platform's.

tools.name: audit_account
tools.description: AI audit of a client's ad account on one platform or all of them. Takes 10-30 seconds. AI: 1 AI request.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

tools.name: audit_google_ads
tools.description: Full Google Ads audit for a client: structure, keywords, responsive search ads, extensions, bidding, conversions and Quality Score problems, with a 0-100 score and recommendations. AI: 1 AI request.

tools.name: audit_meta_ads
tools.description: Full Meta Ads audit for a client: funnel structure, audiences, creatives, pixel health, conversion events, audience fatigue and Advantage+ setup. AI: 1 AI request.

tools.name: audit_conversion_goals
tools.description: Check that a client's ads learn from real leads: which Google Ads conversions are primary, whether calls and forms are counted, and campaigns optimising for the wrong goal.

tools.name: audit_tracking
tools.description: Tracking diagnostics for a client: pixel, GA4 and GTM mismatches on the landing page, conversion actions and the other tracking guards in one report.

tools.name: audit_campaign_quality
tools.description: Reads every running Google and Meta campaign of a client from the platform and checks geo, conversions against the bid strategy, moderation, landing pages and search assets.

tools.name: audit_wasted_spend
tools.description: Campaigns that burn budget: spend with zero conversions, CPA above target, no clicks. Returns the amounts lost, in the account currency.

tools.name: audit_campaign_portfolio
tools.description: Health score of every campaign, the ones in a critical state, without conversions, without goals or with stale data. A good first call before a deeper audit.

tools.name: audit_campaign_health
tools.description: A 1-10 health score for each campaign of a client with the problems behind it.

tools.name: audit_performance_coach
tools.description: A prioritised optimisation plan for a client's last 7 days from four specialist reviews (media buying, budget, audience, creative), with a confidence level per item. Recommendations only. Takes up to a minute. AI: 1 AI request.

tools.name: audit_ad_disapprovals
tools.description: Ads the platforms rejected, with the reason and the policy code.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

status.description: open (default), acknowledged, fixed, wontfix or all.

tools.name: recommendation_list
tools.description: Open recommendation cards: agent advice and Meta's own cabinet advice, judged against the client's goal.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

tools.name: campaign_search
tools.description: Campaigns filtered by client, platform, status or a substring of the name.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

name_filter.description: Case-insensitive substring of the campaign name.

tools.name: campaign_analyze
tools.description: Deep analysis of one campaign: metrics, trends and recommendations. Takes up to a minute. AI: 1 AI request.

campaign_id.description: ADS Beast id from list_campaigns, not the platform's.

tools.name: campaign_diagnose
tools.description: Works through the possible causes of one KPI problem in a campaign: audience saturation, creative fatigue, landing page, bid strategy, seasonality, tracking.

campaign_id.description: ADS Beast id from list_campaigns, not the platform's.

tools.name: campaign_history_analysis
tools.description: What worked for a client before: average CPA and CTR, best campaigns and best audiences.

tools.name: campaign_type_coverage
tools.description: Which campaign types ADS Beast supports on each platform and how far: creation through the API, generation, validation.

platform.description: google, meta, tiktok, linkedin or microsoft.

tools.name: campaign_strategy_generate
tools.description: A strategic plan for a client over a horizon: channels, budget split, KPI targets and launch phases. Takes up to a minute. AI: 1 AI request. May return a job_id (get_job_result).

tools.name: campaign_strategy_expert_review
tools.description: Six specialist viewpoints (media buyer, copywriter, audience, competitors, conversion, data) on a planned campaign. Takes up to a minute. AI: 1 AI request. May return a job_id (get_job_result).

budget_monthly.description: Planned monthly budget in the account currency, whole units.

geo.description: Country code, e.g. us or de.

tools.name: campaign_swarm_runs
tools.description: Recent multi-agent campaign generation runs with status, platform and budget.

tools.name: campaign_draft_details
tools.description: A campaign draft in full: platform, type, goal, budget, UTM, targeting, ad groups with keywords and ads, and the platform campaign id once it was published.

tools.name: campaign_draft_publish_check
tools.description: Validates a campaign draft against the live ad account and reports exactly what publishing would create or change. Read-only rehearsal: nothing is written.

platform_campaign_id.description: Existing platform campaign to complete instead of creating a new one.

tools.name: google_ads_ad_strength
tools.description: Ad Strength of a client's responsive search ads: counts by level and the weak ads with Google's own action items.

force_refresh.description: true queries Google live instead of using the stored snapshot.

tools.name: google_ads_keyword_overlap
tools.description: Finds the same keyword and match type enabled in two or more active Google campaigns of one account. Detection only.

tools.name: google_ads_script_generate
tools.description: Returns a ready Google Ads Script (JavaScript) for one campaign that a person pastes into Google Ads themselves. The tool only produces text. Amounts are in the ad account's own currency, in whole units (not cents or micros).

campaign_id.description: ADS Beast id from list_campaigns, not the platform's.

new_value.description: New value for the update actions: monthly budget, target CPA or target ROAS.

tools.name: google_ads_conversion_tracking_check
tools.description: Reads a client's Google Ads conversion actions and tag and reports which action fits the named conversion, or what would be created. Read-only.

account_id.description: Google account id; needed only when the client has several.

tools.name: google_ads_app_videos_check
tools.description: Reads a Google App campaign and validates the videos proposed for it. Read-only.

account_id.description: Google account id; needed only when the client has several.

campaign_id.description: Google Ads id of the App campaign (digits).

youtube_videos.description: Ids or links of videos already on YouTube.

tools.name: meta_ads_account_setup
tools.description: Pixels, pages, lead forms and conversion events of a client's Meta ad account.

tools.name: meta_ads_interest_search
tools.description: Targeting interests matching a keyword, with id, name, audience size and topic.

query.description: Keyword, for example fitness or real estate.

tools.name: meta_ads_learning_phase
tools.description: Learning status of every active ad set of a client, with what holds learning back.

campaign_id.description: Meta's own campaign id, to check one campaign only.

target_cpa_usd.description: Target CPA, used to judge whether budgets are sufficient.

tools.name: meta_ads_placement_safety_check
tools.description: Shows which ad sets of a client's active Meta campaigns still run on fraud-prone placements and what the safe targeting would be. Read-only.

include_bot_audience.description: Also plan the bot exclusion audience.

tools.name: tiktok_ads_account_setup
tools.description: Pixels, identities and account details of a client's TikTok ad account.

tools.name: linkedin_ads_account_setup
